rows.grounds: Compound describing dimensions: ṣaṭtriṃśat-aṅgula-āyāma (length of thirty-six fingers) and aṣṭa-aṅgula-su-vistara (width of eight fingers).

items.question: What are the prescribed length and width measurements for this ritual implement?
premises: The implement has a specified length.
The length measures thirty-six fingers.
The width measures eight fingers.
items.inference: The ritual implement must be made thirty-six fingers long and eight fingers wide.
items.plain_english: It should be thirty-six fingers in length and eight fingers in width.

rows.grounds: Compound/phrase: vistāreṇa ca dairghyeṇa (in width and length) sūkara-ānana-sannibham (resembling a boar's face).

items.question: What shape must the implement resemble in its overall width and length?
premises: The implement is described by width and length.
Its form is compared to a known shape.
The comparison is to a boar's face.
items.inference: In both width and length the implement should resemble the face of a boar.
items.plain_english: In its width and length, it should resemble the face of a boar.

rows.grounds: Specifies ear dimensions: karṇa-dairghyam (ear length) dvi-mātram (two measures) syāt (should be), vistāram (width) catur-aṅgulam (four fingers).

items.question: What specific length and width are prescribed for the ear portion?
premises: The ear portion has a prescribed length.
The ear length should be two measures.
The ear width should be four fingers.
items.inference: The ear of the implement must be two measures long and four fingers wide.
uncertainties: The exact unit denoted by mātra in this context is not specified.
items.plain_english: The ear should be two measures in length and four fingers in width.

rows.grounds: Alternative measures and feature: tri-mātram vā catur-mātram (three or four measures), tan-madhye (in its middle), bilam ucyate (a hole is called/prescribed).

items.question: What alternative size and central feature are specified for this part of the implement?
premises: An alternative measurement is allowed.
The measure may be three or four measures.
A hole is prescribed in its middle.
items.inference: The part may measure three or four measures and must have a hole in its middle.
uncertainties: The exact unit denoted by mātra in this context is not specified.
items.plain_english: It may be three or four measures, and a hole is prescribed in its middle.

rows.grounds: Instruction on increment: ardha-ardha-aṅgula-vṛddhyā (by increase of a quarter finger), tu (but/indeed), kartavyam (to be made), catur-aṅgulam (four fingers).

items.question: How should the measurement be increased to reach the prescribed four-finger size?
premises: An incremental increase is prescribed.
The increase proceeds by a quarter finger.
The resulting size should be four fingers.
items.inference: The implement should be made four fingers by increasing in increments of a quarter finger.
items.plain_english: It should be made four fingers, increasing by a quarter finger at a time.

rows.grounds: Relates sruk and sruva: sruk syāt (there should be a sruk), sruve api (also in the sruva), tad-yoniḥ (its source/origin), tan-mānam (that measure), tatas tataḥ bhavet (should be from that).

items.question: How is the measurement of the sruva ladle derived in relation to the sruk ladle?
premises: Both sruk and sruva ladles are discussed.
The sruva shares the same source or basis as the sruk.
The sruva's measure should be derived from that basis.
items.inference: The sruva ladle should have its measure derived from the same basis as the sruk ladle.
uncertainties: The exact derivation implied by tatas tataḥ is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The sruk should be made, and the sruva likewise should have its measure derived from the same source.

rows.grounds: Specifies handle dimensions: ṣaḍ-aṅgula-parīṇāhaḥ (six-finger circumference), daṇḍa-mūle (at the base of the handle), ca puṣkare (and at the lotus/bowl).

items.question: What circumference is prescribed for the handle base and the lotus portion?
premises: The handle base has a prescribed circumference.
The lotus portion is included in the specification.
The circumference should be six fingers.
items.inference: Both the base of the handle and the lotus portion should have a circumference of six fingers.
items.plain_english: The circumference should be six fingers at the base of the handle and at the lotus.

rows.grounds: Describes the ghee receptacle: gopura-ākāra-vat (like a tower/gateway), kāryam (to be made), ājya-sthānam (place for ghee), tad-agrake (at its tip).

items.question: What shape and location are prescribed for the receptacle that holds ghee?
premises: A place for ghee must be fashioned.
It should be shaped like a tower.
It should be located at the tip.
items.inference: The ghee receptacle at the tip should be made in the shape of a tower.
items.plain_english: The place for ghee at its tip should be made in the shape of a tower.

rows.grounds: Preference rule: nūtanam karaṇam śreṣṭham (a new implement is best), purāṇam tad-abhāvataḥ (an old one in its absence).

items.question: Which type of ritual implement is preferred when both new and old options exist?
premises: A new implement is considered best.
An old implement is an alternative.
The old implement is used only in the absence of a new one.
items.inference: A newly made implement is preferred, and an old one may be used only if a new one is unavailable.
items.plain_english: A new implement is best; an old one may be used only if a new one is not available.

rows.grounds: Condition for use: tad-ājñā-pūrvakam (preceded by that command/authorization), sa syāt (it should be), tad-bhogya-karaṇam (that implement for use/enjoyment), tataḥ (then).

items.question: Under what condition may an existing implement be used for ritual enjoyment?
premises: Use of the implement requires prior authorization.
The authorization must precede its use.
Only then may it serve as the implement for use.
items.inference: An implement may be used for ritual enjoyment only after receiving the proper prior authorization.
uncertainties: The source or nature of the required command (ājñā) is not specified.
items.plain_english: It should be used only after prior authorization, and then it may serve as the implement for enjoyment.

rows.grounds: Establishes precedent: yena śāstreṇa (by which scripture), yat-sthāne (in which place), kriyā pūrvam pravartate (the rite previously proceeds/is conducted).

items.question: What determines the authoritative precedent for how a ritual is first conducted?
premises: A ritual follows a particular scripture.
A ritual is conducted in a particular place.
The prior practice in that context sets the precedent.
items.inference: The scripture and place according to which a rite was previously conducted establish its authoritative precedent.
items.plain_english: The rite follows the scripture and the place according to which it was previously conducted.

rows.grounds: Rule for gaps: anuktam (what is unstated), anyataḥ grāhyam (to be taken from elsewhere), utsava-ādiṣu karmasu (in festivals and other rites).

items.question: How should ritual details not specified in the primary source be supplied during festivals?
premises: Some ritual details may be unstated in the primary source.
Festivals and other rites still require complete procedures.
Unstated details may be taken from elsewhere.
items.inference: In festivals and other rites, details not stated in the primary source should be adopted from other authoritative sources.
items.plain_english: Whatever is not stated should be taken from elsewhere in festivals and other rites.

rows.grounds: Restriction on borrowing: śreṣṭhaḥ tad-dhāma-saṃsiddhaḥ (best, accomplished in that place), na grāhyaḥ anya-ālaya-sthitaḥ (not to be taken if situated in another shrine).

items.question: Why should an accomplished object from another shrine not be adopted despite its excellence?
premises: An object may be excellent and accomplished in its own place.
Such an object may be situated in another shrine.
Objects from other shrines should not be taken.
items.inference: Even an excellent object accomplished in its own place must not be taken if it belongs to another shrine.
items.plain_english: Even if it is excellent and accomplished in its own place, an object situated in another shrine should not be taken.

rows.grounds: Conditional case: tat-liṅga-ādi-anukūlam cet (if favorable to that sign/emblem etc.), bera-ādyam yat pratiṣṭhitam (whatever image etc. is established).

items.question: Under what condition may an already established image be considered acceptable?
premises: An image or similar object may already be established.
Its suitability depends on compatibility with the deity's sign and related features.
Favorable compatibility is the stated condition.
items.inference: An established image may be acceptable if it is favorable and compatible with the deity's sign and related characteristics.
items.plain_english: If an established image or the like is favorable and compatible with that deity's sign and other features, it may be considered.

rows.grounds: Prescribes remedy: sthānāt sthāna-antara-prāpti-doṣa-śuddhi-artham (for purification of the defect of transfer from one place to another), ācaret (one should perform).

items.question: What ritual action is required when a sacred object is transferred from one place to another?
premises: Transfer from one place to another can cause a defect.
Such a defect requires purification.
A ritual action should be performed for that purification.
items.inference: When a sacred object is moved from one place to another, one should perform rites to purify the defect caused by the transfer.
items.plain_english: One should perform rites to purify the defect arising from transferring it from one place to another.

rows.grounds: Specifies the rite: hrasva-prāsāda-mantreṇa (with the short prāsāda mantra), prabhūta-yajana-anvitam (accompanied by abundant worship).

items.question: What mantra and form of worship should accompany the purification after transfer?
premises: The purification rite requires a specific mantra.
The short prāsāda mantra is prescribed.
The rite must be accompanied by abundant worship.
items.inference: The purification should be performed with the short prāsāda mantra and accompanied by abundant worship.
uncertainties: The exact form of the short prāsāda mantra is not specified here.
items.plain_english: It should be accompanied by abundant worship using the short prāsāda mantra.

rows.grounds: Specifies height range: pañca-ṣaṭ-sapta-hastāni (five, six, or seven cubits), kanyasānām (of the maidens/smaller structures), samucchrayaḥ (height).

items.question: What height range is prescribed for the structures designated as kanyasa?
premises: The kanyasa structures have a prescribed height.
The height may be five cubits.
The height may alternatively be six or seven cubits.
items.inference: The height of the kanyasa structures should be five, six, or seven cubits.
uncertainties: The exact referent of kanyasānām (maidens/smallest class) depends on architectural context.
items.plain_english: The height of the kanyasa structures should be five, six, or seven cubits.

rows.grounds: Further specification: teṣu (among them), hastāt paraḥ (beyond a cubit), khyātaḥ (known), sva-vṛddhi-arha-upalakṣitaḥ (marked as fit for its own increase).

items.question: How may the prescribed height be extended beyond the stated cubit measures?
premises: The stated measures allow extension.
An increase beyond a cubit is recognized.
The extension must be appropriate to its own proportional increase.
items.inference: Among these, an increase beyond the cubit measure is recognized when marked as appropriate to its own proportional growth.
uncertainties: The precise rule for proportional increase is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Among these, an increase beyond the cubit is recognized, marked as appropriate for its own proportional growth.

rows.grounds: Alternative measures: śalya-vasu-aṅgulān vā atha (three or eight fingers, or else), pareṣām (of others), ṣoḍaśa-aṅgulam (sixteen fingers). Uses numerical synonyms śalya (3) and vasu (8).

items.question: What alternative finger-based measurements are prescribed for other cases?
premises: Alternative measurements are given for other cases.
One option is three or eight fingers.
Another option for others is sixteen fingers.
items.inference: For other cases, the measure may be three or eight fingers, or sixteen fingers.
uncertainties: The identification of śalya as three and vasu as eight follows common numerical synonymy but is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Alternatively, for others it may be three or eight fingers, or sixteen fingers.

rows.grounds: Another alternative: udaya-ardha-pramāṇam vā (or half the measure of the rise), yādau ādau paripaṭhyate (as is recited at the beginning/such as first stated).

items.question: What alternative proportional measure is authorized according to earlier prescription?
premises: An alternative proportional measure is allowed.
The measure may be half the rise.
This follows what is recited at the beginning.
items.inference: Alternatively, the measure may be half the rise, as prescribed in the earlier enumeration.
uncertainties: The reading yādādau is slightly unclear; taken as referring to what is stated at the beginning.
items.plain_english: Or it may be half the measure of the rise, as is prescribed at the beginning.

rows.grounds: Introductory injunction: saukhya-karma prakartavyam (the rite for well-being is to be performed), yathāvat śṛṇuta dvijāḥ (listen properly, O twice-born ones).

items.question: What instruction introduces the proper performance of the rite for well-being?
premises: A rite for well-being is to be performed.
The performance must follow proper procedure.
The twice-born are instructed to listen.
items.inference: The rite for well-being must be performed properly, and the twice-born are called to listen to its procedure.
items.plain_english: The rite for well-being is to be performed properly; listen, O twice-born ones.

rows.grounds: Mythic account: sasarja apsarasaḥ (created the apsaras), rudraḥ (Rudra), kauśika-prīti-kāraṇāt (for the sake of Kauśika's pleasure).

items.question: For whose pleasure did Rudra create the celestial nymphs according to this account?
premises: Rudra created the celestial nymphs.
The creation had a specific purpose.
The purpose was to bring pleasure to Kauśika.
items.inference: Rudra created the celestial nymphs for the sake of Kauśika's pleasure.
uncertainties: The identity of Kauśika is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Rudra created the celestial nymphs for the sake of Kauśika's pleasure.

rows.grounds: States a condition: aspṛśyam (untouchable), pratiloma-ādyaiḥ (by those of reverse order and others), ajāyata (was born/arose), sanātanam (eternal).

items.question: What enduring status arose in relation to those born of reverse social order?
premises: A condition of untouchability is described.
It relates to those of reverse order and others.
This condition is characterized as eternal.
items.inference: An eternal condition of being untouchable by those of reverse order and others came into being.
uncertainties: The syntactic subject of ajāyata is compressed and not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: An eternal state arose, untouchable by those of reverse birth and others.

rows.grounds: Locates a past event: devatā-aru-vane (in the grove of the deity), pūrvam (before), vinoda-artham (for the sake of amusement), mayā purā (by me formerly).

items.question: Where and for what purpose did the speaker act in the earlier time described?
premises: The speaker refers to a former action.
The action took place in the deity's grove.
The purpose of the action was amusement.
items.inference: The speaker formerly acted in the deity's grove for the sake of amusement.
uncertainties: The specific action performed is not stated in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Formerly, in the deity's grove, I did this for the sake of amusement.
